beats: Hook (line_qc_perfect_ledger_double): describing 50 interacting electrons exactly on a classical computer takes 2^50, about a quadrillion, complex numbers (check: about 18 PB at 16 bytes each); add one electron and the count doubles: every stack is twice the one before. Cast for all of QC01 (the six parts cut from her first lecture, Q25-01): the physicist (older, bald with a fluffy fringe, bushy moustache, goggles pushed up, lab coat) and the student (lanky, a tuft of hair, round glasses, striped long-sleeved T-shirt, messenger bag); both invented. No lecturer figure anywhere and never her likeness: her voice and her slides carry her part.
Nature does it effortlessly; could a computer made of the same stuff? (line_qc_perfect_nature_easy; the early 1980s: Feynman 1982, Deutsch 1985; the slide marks 1983, say "the early 1980s").
Wave 1 imagines a perfect machine: unlimited qubits, perfect gates, no cold; even then, is it worth building, and for what? (line_qc_perfect_dream_machine; tape p9; clip 20:20-20:45).
Quantum data: n two-state particles need a state vector of 2^n numbers, and every step a 2^n x 2^n matrix, on a classical machine (back to line_qc_perfect_ledger_double; clip 23:31-24:26).

Classical data with hidden structure: factoring (21 = 3 x 7). Multiplying is quick, undoing it is slow for big numbers, and much of today's encryption rests on that (line_qc_perfect_factor_tiles; Shor 1994; keep to "much of today's encryption", no security or state framing).

Why classical simulation stops near 50 qubits even on supercomputers: one more qubit needs a whole second warehouse (line_qc_perfect_two_warehouses; reuse line_cluster_campus for the supercomputer; clip 56:38-57:05; largest full state-vector simulations ~45-50 qubits, check).
Not every problem speeds up: the quantum key fits only some locks (line_qc_perfect_special_key; points ahead to QC07-01).
Cover (line_qc_cover_01_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the student staggers beside a swaying tower of notebooks while a little molecule floats calmly beside it.
